question: Bohr’s model is only applicable to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Bohr’s Model** is specifically applicable to systems with a **single electron**, such as the **hydrogen atom** or hydrogen-like ions (e.g., He⁺, Li²⁺). It cannot accurately describe multi-electron systems.
 
• The model explains the **quantized energy levels** of electrons in an atom and is most effective for **simpler atomic systems**.
 
• In the case of **hydrogen**, it has only one electron, making it the ideal candidate for the application of Bohr’s theory.
 
• The model assumes that electrons travel in fixed **circular orbits** around the nucleus without radiating
